reasoning_pass1: Code: $filename = $this->generateFileLocation($key); then unserialize(file_get_contents($filename)). CWE-22 (Path Traversal) requires that $key flows to a path with attacker-controlled traversal sequences. Cannot see generateFileLocation in snippet, likely hashes key but unknown. file_exists/is_readable checks present. Insufficient context. Default to FP because cache implementations typically hash keys, but low confidence.

Go backend code in argo-cd applicationset/utils. CWE-79 (XSS) requires HTML output to a browser. Template rendering here is for argo-cd CRD generation (k8s manifests) and YAML/JSON conversion. No browser HTML output context. CWE-79 rule mis-fired on text/template usage. Language field says 'javascript' but file is .go — additional indicator of rule misclass.

CodeIgniter4 debug toolbar (system/Debug/Toolbar/Views/toolbar.js). innerHTML concat with row.innerText and route templates. Debug toolbars are developer-only; routes shown are from user's own application code (trusted at dev time), not external untrusted input. Even though innerHTML+concat looks XSS-shaped, the data source is not attacker-controllable in this context. Confidence MEDIUM because debug bars sometimes leak into prod accidentally.

unserialize(file_get_contents($filename)) on $filename derived from $key via generateFileLocation. CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data) is exactly this pattern. Exploit: if attacker controls $key path (cache poisoning) or can write the cache file directly, deserialization triggers gadget chain. PHP unserialize without HMAC/signing is a recognized vulnerability. Need to see if $key is sanitized in generateFileLocation; without that, this is a real vulnerability pattern. Verdict TP.

CWE-918 (SSRF) claim is wrong for this code. SSRF is about server fetching attacker-controlled URLs. This code does dynamic require_once + new $controller() + $controllerObject->$function() — that's CWE-94 (Code Injection) or CWE-470 (Unsafe Reflection), NOT SSRF. Semgrep rule misfired. From rule's claimed-CWE perspective, this is FP. Note: code IS vulnerable to RCE via dynamic class loading (the whitelist guards $function but not $controller path), real_cwe should be CWE-94.

Java Spring auth filter. response.getWriter().print(SecurityUtils.generateJWToken(...).serialize()) outputs a JWT token to TEXT_PLAIN response. JWT is base64-encoded structured data with HMAC signature. Content-Type set to text/plain before write. No HTML/JS rendering context. CWE-79 (XSS) requires browser interpretation as markup, doesn't apply to JWT in text/plain response.

Same unserialize(file_get_contents(generateFileLocation($key))) pattern as hl_5d63cd05 (WeGIA Cache.php). PHP unsafe deserialization pattern when filename or content can be attacker-influenced. Cache write/read with attacker-controlled keys = gadget chain risk. Real vulnerability pattern.

yeswiki language detection. unserialize($_POST['config']) is called BUT for PHP 7+: ['allowed_classes' => false] flag is set — this blocks object instantiation, neutralizing gadget chain attacks. For PHP <7: custom regex preprocessing transforms O:/C: serialize markers to __PHP_Incomplete_Class to neutralize object injection. Both branches show defensive intent. Pattern looks dangerous but mitigations are in place. Modern PHP runs allowed_classes=false; deployment without PHP 7+ in 2024+ is rare.

$almox = $_REQUEST['almox']; then directly concatenated into mysqli_query SQL string: WHERE estoque.id_almoxarifado=$almox. No parameterization, no escaping, no type check. Classic CWE-89 SQL injection. Attacker sends ?almox=1 OR 1=1-- to dump all stock data. Severity higher than MEDIUM in practice.

yeswiki ConfigurationFile loads config via eval() of file contents (str_replace + eval). That's a code-injection-via-eval pattern (CWE-95) not CWE-78 (OS Command Injection). The actual code is dangerous if $this->_file is attacker-controlled, but claimed CWE is wrong. Semgrep rule misclass on CWE label. real_cwe should be CWE-95.

File is docs/docs/_static/js/algolia.js — minified third-party Algolia DocSearch library bundled into llama_index documentation site. Header comment confirms 'Original file: /npm/@docsearch/js@3.6.1/dist/umd/index.js'. Semgrep CWE-79 rule fired on minified vendor JS. Not project code. Pure noise.

Authentik blueprint YAML for OIDC conformance TESTING (path: blueprints/testing/, metadata.name 'OpenID Conformance testing', label blueprints.goauthentik.io/instantiate: 'false' — never auto-applied). Hard-coded client_id and client_secret are intentional test fixture values used to validate OIDC compliance suite. Semgrep CWE-798 rule cannot distinguish test fixtures from production secrets. fp_cause_taxonomy=test_code.

GitHub Actions workflow interpolates github.event.pull_request.title (attacker-controlled — any PR opener can set it) directly into bash via PR_TITLE="${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" and then uses it inside a heredoc double-quoted JSON payload to curl. Classic GitHub Actions context-injection: PR title containing `";$(rm -rf /);#` would break out into shell command execution on runner. This is a documented vulnerability pattern with many real CVEs. Should use intermediate env var or jq for proper escaping.

EspoCRM CLI tool extension.php. Hard guard: if (!str_starts_with(php_sapi_name(), 'cli')) { exit; } — refuses to run via HTTP. Input is $_SERVER['argv'][1], a CLI argument, not HTTP attacker-controlled. CWE-918 (SSRF) claim is nonsensical for a CLI installer that reads a local zip file. No HTTP request based on user input — no SSRF surface at all.

Homebox labelmaker.go imports text/template and os/exec. Snippet shows GenerateParameters struct, Validate, wrapText, etc. — no template.Execute() call or exec.Command() call is visible. CWE-94 (Code Injection) requires a template-with-user-input or eval-style sink. Without seeing the actual sink, default FP — image label generation is unlikely to flow user input into template eval. Need full file to confirm.

llama.cpp simplechat helper: ui.el_create_append_p(`${x.role}: ${x.content}`, div). el_create_append_p is a helper to create+append paragraph element — by convention these use textContent not innerHTML. div.innerHTML = gUsageMsg uses a static config message, not user input. Even if there were a leak, simplechat is local-loopback dev playground, self-XSS at worst. CWE-79 rule firing on template literal looks like syntactic noise.

Same WeGIA controller dispatcher pattern as hl_dc646bc3 (different commit, additional whitelist entry). Dynamic require_once($controllerPath) + new $controller() + $controllerObject->$function(). Real vuln is CWE-94 (Code Injection / Unsafe Reflection), not CWE-918 (SSRF). Claimed CWE wrong; from rule's perspective FP.

MobSF execute_adb endpoint: authenticated POST with cmd=request.POST['cmd'] passed via subprocess.Popen(args + cmd.split(' '), ...) with NO shell=True. Has `# lgtm [py/command-line-injection]` comment + 'Expected, cmd execute inside VM/AVD' — author intentionally exposes ADB shell for security analysts. Auth-gated (login_required, Permissions.SCAN), targeted at VM sandbox. Intentional feature, not a real exploit path from external untrusted input. fp_cause_taxonomy=framework_protection.

WeGIA map theme.js preview() builds previewHtml from this.$wrapper.find('[data-builder-field="mapid"]').val() — user-typed mapid value — and concats it into innerHTML string for iframe.body. Also concats this.generate() into a customScript.text which is then appended to iframe — if generate() returns user-influenced content this is CWE-79 (DOM XSS). Self-XSS at minimum; stored XSS if mapid persists and other users see preview.

dbgate main.js: snippet shows just BASIC_AUTH setup and authorizer. CWE-352 (CSRF) is 'absence-of-token' style — Semgrep is firing on a setup block that does not include csrf-middleware. For basic auth, modern browsers block cross-origin Authorization headers, mitigating CSRF for the auth itself. If session cookies are issued post-auth, CSRF is possible — cannot tell from this slice. Default to FP because (a) basic auth context is not classical CSRF target, (b) CWE-352 detectors are infamous false-positive-prone.

gpt_academic Social_Helper.py snippet shows friend.friends_list iteration, msg construction, run_gpt_fn lambda — pure in-memory Python with chatbot/llm objects. No pickle.loads, yaml.unsafe_load, marshal.loads, or other CWE-502 sink visible. Semgrep likely fired on imports or pattern-matched against typical pickle keywords. Note: line range '86-85' is start>end which suggests Semgrep self-confusion.

WeGIA admin update endpoint runs exec('git -C '.ROOT.' pull 2>&1'). ROOT is a hardcoded constant (defined elsewhere in app, not user input). No part of the exec string comes from $_REQUEST/$_POST/$_GET. CWE-94 (Code Injection) requires user input flowing into code-eval sink. Intentional admin self-update feature. Confidence MEDIUM because absence of auth check in this snippet leaves room for unauthenticated RCE risk if .htaccess/router rules are wrong, but the CWE-94 claim itself is wrong.

llama_index BaseObjectNodeMapping abstract base class. Snippet shows `import pickle` and exception handling for `pickle.PickleError`, but no actual `pickle.load()` or `pickle.loads()` invocation visible — only abstract method definitions. CWE-502 needs a concrete deserialization sink. Abstract class with pickle-aware error handling is not itself vulnerable. Subclasses may or may not be.

EspoCRM SchemaManager runSql() iterates $queries array and calls $connection->executeQuery($sql). The queries are schema migration SQL generated internally by Doctrine DBAL's schema diff/introspection layer — not user input. Semgrep fires on raw executeQuery() without prepared statements, but this is intentional admin schema management with internally-generated SQL strings.

ClipBucket upload_user_file: $file_name = $uid . '.' . $ext where $uid is validated by $userquery->user_exists($uid) (likely a numeric DB ID) and $ext comes from getext($file['name']) which typically returns just the suffix after the last dot. After move_uploaded_file, ValidateImage check unlinks invalid files. Path traversal requires $ext or $uid to contain traversal sequences — unlikely if both are properly typed/validated. LOW confidence because getext semantics depend on its implementation.

Two SQL queries with direct concatenation of $_POST values: DELETE FROM funcionario_dependentes WHERE id_dependente = $id_dependente AND SELECT WHERE fdep.id_funcionario = $_POST['id_funcionario']. Classic CWE-89 SQL injection in both. Auth check exists ($_SESSION['usuario'] and permissao) but does not sanitize $_POST inputs. Attacker with low-privilege session can dump tables and chain DELETE statements.

vim/Filelist is the Vim source distribution Makefile manifest listing source files included in tarball releases. Not executable code — just a list of strings with backslash continuations. Semgrep firing CWE-22 (Path Traversal) on a manifest is nonsense; there is no file-open sink, no user input, no traversal possible. Pure rule-misfire on text content.

MobSF firebase.py open_firebase(): does perform requests.get() to a user-supplied url, but: (a) valid_host(url) check, (b) purl.netloc.endswith('.firebaseio.com') restricts target domain, (c) allow_redirects=False prevents redirect-based SSRF bypass. Intentional feature of MobSF (detecting OPEN Firebase DBs in scanned APKs). Note: endswith check could be bypassed (e.g. 'evil.com.firebaseio.com' or '@victim/'.firebaseio.com'), so SSRF is not 100% impossible. Going FP because (a) intended feature, (b) MobSF is a security analyzer where outgoing requests are expected.

WeGIA upload endpoint uses DENYLIST approach: $bloqueados = ['php', 'exe', 'sh', 'bat', 'js', 'html', 'htm']. Missing critical extensions: phtml, php3, php4, php5, php7, pht, phar — all of which can trigger PHP execution on Apache+mod_php default configurations. Destination directory '../tabelas/' is web-accessible (confirmed by '$r[url] = ./tabelas/' return). Attacker uploads shell.phtml or shell.phar, accesses /tabelas/shell.phtml to gain RCE. Classic CWE-434 (Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type) via incomplete denylist.

conda_build convert.py: tarfile.open(file_path).extractall(temporary_directory) — extractall WITHOUT a filter is the canonical TarSlip / Zip Slip CWE-22 pattern. Malicious tar entries with absolute paths or '../' sequences can write files outside temporary_directory. Known Python tarfile vulnerability addressed by PEP 706 (Python 3.12+ requires explicit filter). file_path comes from CLI input to conda-build. Classic FP-vs-TP gray: well-known pattern, exploitable if attacker-supplied tar.

WeGIA adicionar_status_atendido.php takes $_POST['status'], passes to prepared statement via bindParam, executes. No HTML output anywhere in this script. The only echo is $e->getMessage() in catch (PDO error message). CWE-79 (XSS) requires reflection of user input back to HTML/JS context — absent here. Semgrep CWE-79 misfire on any $_POST read.

Lychee SecurePathController has TRIPLE gate before path access: (a) signature expiration check, (b) request->hasValidSignature() (Laravel signed URL HMAC), (c) optional Crypt::decryptString($path) before file access. Storage::disk(LOCAL)->path($path) then resolves within configured disk root. Attacker cannot forge a signed URL without knowing app key. CWE-22 claim ignores all three controls. Real risk only if signed URL secret leaks (out of scope).

llama_index CLI RAG base.py snippet shows QueryPipeline construction, field_validator for chat_engine, CondenseQuestionChatEngine.from_defaults — pure LLM pipeline builder code. No subprocess/os.system/exec/popen calls. CWE-78 (OS Command Injection) requires a shell-execution sink that does not exist in this snippet. Rule misfire.
WeGIA adicionar_situacao.php — same pattern as hl_7da4e72c. $_POST['situacao'] → prepared statement bindParam → execute. No HTML output. CWE-79 (XSS) claim absent — no reflection sink in this script.

yeswiki deletepage.php builds HTML: '<form action="' . $cancelUrl . '" method="post"...' where $cancelUrl = $incomingurl, which comes from urldecode($_GET['incomingurl']). NO htmlentities/htmlspecialchars on $cancelUrl before placing into attribute context. Attacker can craft incomingurl that breaks out of the attribute with a quote and injects onmouseover= or similar. CWE-79 attribute-context XSS is real. The csrf-token is htmlentities'd but the URL is not.

navidrome artist_repository.go: roleFilter() formats role into SQL JSON-path fragment via fmt.Sprintf("stats ->> '$.%v'", role) used as map key in NotEq{}. Role parameter is `any` and could carry untrusted data if called from API context. But the typical Subsonic role enum is a small fixed set ('admin', 'user', 'guest'), and roleFilter is registered as a known query-builder filter — likely called only with internal enum values. Without seeing the caller, default to FP based on contextual prior.

Craft CMS UpdaterController::actionRestoreDb: Craft::$app->getDb()->restore($this->data['dbBackupPath']). $this->data is server-side updater session state set during the previous update step, not raw user input. restore() executes the configured DB restore command on a known backup file path. Intentional admin-only updater functionality, auth-gated at framework level. CWE-94 (Code Injection) doesn't fit — this is database file restore, not code evaluation.

WeGIA MedicamentoControle adicionarMedicamento(): var_dump($_REQUEST); extract($_REQUEST); c->adicionarMedicamento($nomeMedicamento, $descricaoMedicamento, $aplicacaoMedicamento). extract($_REQUEST) is a security anti-pattern (variable injection CWE-915) and passes $_REQUEST values straight to DAO method. Need to inspect SaudePetDAO::adicionarMedicamento to verify it uses prepared statements. Given WeGIA pattern (many confirmed concatenation-based SQLi findings in this same repo), prior is HIGH that DAO concats. Going TP.

WeGIA cargos.php has unparameterized SQL using $_SESSION['id_pessoa'] (session value, not attacker-controlled directly unless session-jacked) — that's CWE-89 risk, not CWE-79. HTML section uses display_campo() (server-side template render). No echo of user-controlled input visible in this snippet. CWE-79 (XSS) claim doesn't fit — would have been CWE-89 for the SQL, if anything.

WeGIA QuadroHorarioControle.adicionarEscala() catches PDOException and echo("Erro ao adicionar escala '$escala' ..." . $e->getMessage()). $escala is filter_input(INPUT_POST, 'escala', FILTER_SANITIZE_STRING) — FILTER_SANITIZE_STRING is DEPRECATED in PHP 8.1 and behaves as a no-op on modern versions. If attacker triggers a DB error (e.g. with invalid input), the unescaped $escala is echoed back to HTML response = stored or reflected XSS. Additional open redirect via header(Location: $nextPage) but that's CWE-601 not CWE-79.

WeGIA Cadastro_Atendido.php reads $cpf = $_GET['cpf']. SQL queries use prepared statements with bind_param. In the visible portion (PHP head + HTML <head> setup), $cpf is NOT echoed into HTML/JS context. The snippet truncates before the form body — XSS could exist further down in the file where $cpf would naturally appear in a form's value attribute. Default to FP based on visible code but solvable_from_snippet=no.

themeisle Elementor pricing-table widget render(): every $settings field is wrapped with esc_html(), esc_attr(), or esc_url() before output. WordPress standard XSS protection used consistently. No raw user-controlled string reaches HTML output.

MobSF forms.py is a Django ModelForm definition (RegisterForm extends UserCreationForm). Form definitions do not render HTML themselves — Django templating layer auto-escapes output. forms.ChoiceField restricts role values to ('viewer', 'maintainer') tuple. CWE-79 rule firing on Django form class is misfire.

llama_index react_agent.py lines 31-33 are just import statements (from llama_index.core.llms.llm import ToolSelection, etc.). No file path manipulation, no os.path/open/Path() operations at the flagged lines. CWE-22 (Path Traversal) requires a path-based sink. Pure rule misfire on import lines.

WeGIA profile_dependente.php uses filter_input(INPUT_GET, 'id_dependente', FILTER_SANITIZE_NUMBER_INT) → validates $id > 0 → passes as parameter to $pdo->prepare with :id_dependente placeholder → execute([':id_dependente' => $id]). Proper parameterized query. CWE-89 (SQL Injection) claim is wrong — this is the secure pattern.

WeGIA QuadroHorarioControle (earlier commit) — same pattern as hl_91f24c5f. extract($_REQUEST) + echo of $escala in PDOException catch handler. Reflected/stored XSS via DB error path. Same vulnerability, earlier code state.

WikiDocs submit.php image_delete_ajax: $image_filename = $_POST['image_name']; $filename = $DOC->DIR . $image_filename; unlink($filename). No sanitization of $image_filename — attacker posts image_name=../../../etc/passwd, getting arbitrary file delete. Auth check exists (autenticationLevel() == 2) so admin-only, but admin can delete files outside document directory. Classic CWE-22 (Path Traversal) in unlink sink.

MediaWiki extension JS: mw.config.get('wgShortDesc') → mw.util.addSubtitle(shortdesc). wgShortDesc is a MediaWiki config value set server-side from page metadata; MediaWiki's mw.util.addSubtitle uses .text() / textContent internally for safe DOM updates (per MW framework convention). MW core sanitizes content properly. Self-XSS-only at worst if config got malicious.

pingvin-share file.service.ts lines 20-24 are imports and class constructor declaration. No file write, no upload handling logic visible. CWE-434 (Unrestricted File Upload) requires a sink that accepts file content and writes to disk without validation — not in flagged region. Solvable_from_snippet=no, default FP.

siyuan-note app/src/asset/anno.ts: PDF page render to canvas, getImageData/putImageData for rect extraction, tempCanvas.toDataURL() to get base64 data URL, fetchPost to setFileAnnotation. Pure canvas image manipulation + JSON.stringify config to backend. No HTML innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/eval anywhere. JSON.parse(response.data.data) for config is structured JSON, not HTML. CWE-79 (XSS) doesn't fit canvas-image-flow code.
